# Publication and history

Publishing the draft, making a saved version live or rolling back to one (only on the human's go), naming a version, and undoing or redoing your own last step.

[`version.snapshot`](#versionsnapshot) · [`publication.publish`](#publicationpublish) · [`version.publish`](#versionpublish) · [`version.rollback`](#versionrollback) · [`history.undo`](#historyundo) · [`history.redo`](#historyredo)

## version.snapshot

Name the site as it is now: a version to publish, compare with or return to. It changes nothing on the site, and undo does not take it back. Refused with `version.exists` when the name is taken.

- **op**; class `publish` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; not undoable.
- Found by the plain words: "snapshot", "version".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string (max 64) | yes | The version's name, as a person calls it (`Nuovo sito 2026`): at most 64 characters, used once, never `live`. |
| `note` | string (min 1, max 1024) |  | What the version holds, in a few words, for whoever reads the list of versions. |

Example input:

```json
{"name":"Nuovo sito 2026","note":"Nuova home, pagina Persone e i lavori di via Giulia"}
```

## publication.publish

Publish the draft: it goes live as the next version (v<N>), all or nothing; the live pages are cleared, the search index rebuilt and the version's screenshots taken. Only on the human's go, alone in a batch with confirmed ["publish"]. Pass baseRevisions as you read the draft: a draft that moved since is refused as stale_revision. A dry run judges it with nothing stored. The same requestId again answers the first publish.

- **door**, alone in its batch; class `publish` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); needs `"confirmed": ["publish"]`; dry_run_ops judges it; not undoable.
- Found by the plain words: "publish", "live", "online".

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `note` | string (max 2000) |  |

Example input:

```json
{"note":"Opening section and team page"}
```

## version.publish

Make a saved version live (`version`, as the versions resource names it), forward only: going back is version.rollback. Only on the human's go, alone in a batch with confirmed ["publish"]; a dry run judges it with nothing stored.

- **door**, alone in its batch; class `publish` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); needs `"confirmed": ["publish"]`; dry_run_ops judges it; not undoable.
- Found by the plain words: "publish", "live", "version".

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | string (min 1, max 64) | yes |

Example input:

```json
{"version":"v12"}
```

## version.rollback

Make live again a version that was live before; the draft keeps the edits made since. The live pages are cleared, the search index rebuilt and the screenshots taken. Only on the human's go, alone in a batch with confirmed ["publish"]; a dry run judges it with nothing stored.

- **door**, alone in its batch; class `rollback` (Administrator); needs `"confirmed": ["publish"]`; dry_run_ops judges it; not undoable.
- Found by the plain words: "live", "rollback", "version".

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | string (min 1, max 64) | yes |

Example input:

```json
{"version":"v11"}
```

## history.undo

Take back your own last step: the newest step of the site's history, when it is yours. Alone in a batch with { step }: the entryId your write answered (its answer offers this call as `undo` while the step is the newest). Refused as stale_step when another step came since, as not_own_step for a step someone else made (a person undos it in History), and with the role refusal when your role could not make the change.

- **door**, alone in its batch; class `write` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); no confirmation; dry_run_ops judges it; not undoable.
- Found by the plain words: "undo", "bring".

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `step` | string (min 1, max 100) | yes |

Example input:

```json
{"step":"<entryId>"}
```

## history.redo

Put your own step back again: the newest undo of the site's history, when the step is yours. Alone in a batch with { step }: the entryId your write answered (its answer offers this call as `redo` while the step is the newest). Refused as stale_step when another step came since, as not_own_step for a step someone else made (a person redos it in History), and with the role refusal when your role could not make the change.

- **door**, alone in its batch; class `write` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); no confirmation; dry_run_ops judges it; not undoable.
- Found by the plain words: "redo".

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `step` | string (min 1, max 100) | yes |

Example input:

```json
{"step":"<entryId>"}
```
